{
 "summary": "Findings: the plan cannot ship phase 1 safely. Phase 1 reads a column that only phase 2 creates, and the plan's own phase-1 check skips the test that would catch this. The rest are gaps in tests and structure.

1. Title: Phase 1 deploys a query against a column that does not exist yet, so the pick list goes down in production
   Severity: P1
   Location: phase-1/t1 (read with phase-2/t1 and the "Each phase is one merge to main and deploys on its own" constraint)
   Failure: phase-1/t1 adds `i.bin_code` to the SQL in SqlItemRepo.linesForOrder (src/items.ts:28). The column is only added by migrations/003_item_bin_code.sql in phase-2/t1. Today items has only sku and name (migrations/001_items.sql:1-4). README.md:13 says every merge deploys at once, migrations first, and "the pick list is in use around the clock". I ran bun:sqlite against that schema and `SELECT i.bin_code ...` throws `SQLiteError: no such column: i.bin_code`. So every pick-list request (getPickList, src/routes.ts:10-11) fails from the phase-1 deploy until phase 2 merges. The phase-1 staging check ("Print the pick list of one order from the staging terminal") would fail the same way. The summary's reason for this order ("pickers gain from it at once") is wrong twice: phase 1 breaks the list, and even after a fix every line shows "-" because nothing can set a bin before phase 2.
   Fix: Move migrations/003_item_bin_code.sql into phase 1, before t1. Or put the migration in its own first phase. Phase 2 then holds only the clerk write path. Drop the summary's claim that pickers benefit at once.

2. Title: Phase-1 verification skips the only test that runs the real SQL
   Severity: P1
   Location: phase-1/verification, phase-1/files, implementation_contract d1
   Failure: Phase 1 is checked only with `bun test tests/picklist.test.ts`. That test uses MemoryItemRepo (tests/picklist.test.ts:3,6), which never touches SQL. tests/sql-item-repo.test.ts:9-10,18 runs migrate and then SqlItemRepo.linesForOrder against SQLite, so it would fail on defect 1. The plan never names that file in any phase, and d1's completion check is only about picklist.test.ts. Even plain `bun test` would just turn red without asserting anything about bin codes. No phase asserts the bin_code to binCode mapping or SqlItemRepo.setBinCode against real SQLite.
   Fix: Add tests/sql-item-repo.test.ts to phase 1 with a scenario "linesForOrder returns binCode null for an unset item and the stored code for a set one". Add it to phase-2/t2 for setBinCode: true for a known sku, false for an unknown sku, null clears. Make the phase-1 verification `bun test`.

3. Title: The "type-checks" scenario cannot be run
   Severity: P2
   Location: phase-1/t1 test_scenarios
   Failure: "The project type-checks with the new field" has no command behind it. package.json:5-7 has only `"test": "bun test"`, there is no typescript dependency or node_modules, and `which tsc` finds nothing. Bun strips types without checking them. So the existing fixtures that will lack the new required field (tests/picklist.test.ts:8-9) are never flagged, and the scenario proves nothing.
   Fix: Replace it with a runtime assertion (see defect 2). Or add a type-check gate as its own task, which is outside this request.

4. Title: The plan does not say the existing rendering test and its fixtures must change
   Severity: P2
   Location: phase-1/t2, phase-1/t1
   Failure: Once binCode is a required field, the fixtures at tests/picklist.test.ts:8-9 no longer match PickLine. Inserting the bin field also changes the expected strings at tests/picklist.test.ts:15-16 (format at src/picklist.ts:8), so the current test fails. The plan lists only new scenarios. It also says "after the line number" without giving the separator. The current line is `${lineNo.padStart(3)}  ${sku.padEnd(10)}  ...`, so the plan's snippet with no two-space gap would run the bin into the sku.
   Fix: Give the exact new line template, for example `${no}  ${(binCode ?? "-").padEnd(6)}  ${sku.padEnd(10)}  x${qty}  ${name}`. Say that the existing test is updated: binCode is added to its fixtures and the expected lines are rewritten. The line-order scenario can extend that existing test instead of adding a new one.

5. Title: Parallel State: MemoryItemRepo copies one item's bin onto every order line, and it diverges from SqlItemRepo for unknown skus
   Severity: P2
   Location: phase-2/t2
   Failure: In SQL the bin is a field of the item (items.bin_code). MemoryItemRepo stores only PickLine arrays per order (tests/memory-item-repo.ts:4). The plan has setBinCode "update binCode on every stored line of that sku", which keeps one item datum in N copies. The memory repo also has no item table, so it would answer "unknown sku" for an item that exists but is on no order. SqlItemRepo answers by items rows (UPDATE ... WHERE sku = ?). Route tests on MemoryItemRepo (phase-2/t3 "unknown sku returns 404") would therefore test behavior that is not production's. The phase-1/t1 claim that MemoryItemRepo "needs no change" holds only because it already mixes item and line data together.
   Fix: Give MemoryItemRepo an items map (sku to name and binCode) plus order lines that reference skus, mirroring the schema. linesForOrder joins them and setBinCode writes the one item entry. Do it in phase 1 so fixtures are built once.

6. Title: The request body shape is not validated, and the wording "whether a row changed" is imprecise
   Severity: P3
   Location: phase-2/t3, phase-2/t2
   Failure: putItemBin takes `body` as `{ binCode: string | null }`, but a terminal body is untrusted. The plan does not say what happens when binCode is missing, a number, or a non-object. "Any other shape is rejected with a message" (REQUEST.md item 2) should cover these, but the plan only tests the string case A-3-2. Separately, my SQLite probe shows `changes` is 1 even when the stored value is unchanged, and 0 only for an unknown sku. So "returns whether a row changed" really means "the sku matched". The implementation is correct, but the description reads wrong.
   Fix: Specify that any binCode that is neither null nor a string passing isBinCode gets the same 400 and message, and add one scenario for it (for example a missing binCode). Reword t2 to "returns whether the sku exists (changes > 0)".

7. Title: The migration scenario has no owning test
   Severity: P3
   Location: phase-2/t1 test_scenarios
   Failure: "migrate applies cleanly to an empty database" names no test file. Only tests/sql-item-repo.test.ts:10 runs migrate, and the plan never touches that file.
   Fix: Let the SqlItemRepo bin-code scenarios from defect 2 own this; they run migrate in beforeEach. Drop the separate scenario.

Verified correct: src/db.ts:8-11 applies *.sql files in sorted file-name order, so 003 runs after 002. getPickList and renderPickList take the ItemRepo port (src/routes.ts:10, src/picklist.ts:4). SQL lives only in SqlItemRepo. The ORDER BY l.line_no (src/items.ts:31) and the memory sort (tests/memory-item-repo.ts:7) keep line order. The isBinCode regex /^[A-Z]-\d{2}-\d$/ matches the stated shape and the listed rejections. routes.ts has no router (plain functions with path comments), so adding putItemBin as a function fits that pattern.",

}

 "summary": "Findings: 2 P1 and 3 P2 defects. The plan should not be implemented as written. Baseline is `bun test`: 3 pass, 0 fail. Probes I ran: normalizePhone("12345") returns "12345" and normalizePhone("07700 900123") returns "07700900123". 2027-01-12T09:30Z formats as 09:30 in both UTC and Europe/London, and 02:30 in America/Denver.

1. Title: normalizePhone never returns null and does not validate. Severity P1. Location: phase-2/t1, and context.key_files (the phone.ts entry).
Failure: The plan says normalizePhone "returns null when the input is not a valid mobile number" and turns input into E.164. It also says "A null result covers both the missing and the invalid number, so no separate validation is needed." The code says otherwise: src/patients/phone.ts:2-4 is `normalizePhone(raw: string): string` and only strips the characters `\s-().`. It can never return null and returns no E.164 form ("07700900123", not "+447700900123"). With the plan's code, `mobile !== null` is always true when a mobile exists. "12345" and every landline would be sent to the gateway, which bills every attempt (src/sms/gateway.ts:1). That breaks request item 1, "Never send an SMS to an invalid number". It also makes the plan's own "12345 gets no SMS" scenario fail.
Fix: Add a task that adds a real mobile-number validator and E.164 conversion, returning null for invalid or non-mobile input. Keep normalizePhone's signature unchanged: README.md:8 says the SMS gateway is already used for sign-in codes, and that code is not in this repo. Changing normalizePhone could break those callers, so add a new function next to it. Test it directly: valid, invalid, too short, landline and formatted input.

2. Title: The rule for a "valid mobile number" and its country is undecided. Severity P1 (design blocker). Location: phase-2/t1 and open_questions (which is empty).
Failure: Numbers are stored "as the patient typed it" (src/patients/patients.ts:5-6), for example the national-format "07700 900123" (tests/pass.test.ts:6). Clinics sit in different zones (src/clinics.ts:4 gives "America/Denver"; README.md:3 says each clinic has its own zone). So turning a national number into E.164, and deciding mobile versus landline, needs a default country. No entity in the code carries one: Clinic has no country field. The plan never decides this.
Fix: List it in open_questions for the practice managers or the design. Options: a country per clinic, a single practice country, or accept only numbers stored in international form. Write the validator task only after that is answered.

3. Title: The time-zone tests use Europe/London in January, which equals UTC. Severity P2. Location: phase-1/t1 test_scenarios, phase-1/t2, and directive d1.
Failure: The probe shows 09:30Z prints 09:30 in both UTC and Europe/London on 2027-01-12. The scenario "formatSlot(..., 'Europe/London') is 'Tue 12 Jan 2027, 09:30': this proves the clinic's time zone is applied" proves nothing. A formatSlot that ignores timeZone and keeps the hard-coded "UTC" (src/format.ts:4) still passes. Same for t2 with tests/pass.test.ts:5,11. Request item 3 is about clinics outside UTC, and no test covers one.
Fix: Add a non-UTC case: formatSlot(2027-01-12T09:30:00Z, "America/Denver") is "Tue 12 Jan 2027, 02:30". Optionally add a case where the date also changes. In tests/pass.test.ts, add an appointment at a non-UTC clinic and assert that both the email body and the SMS text contain the local time. The plan never asserts local time in the SMS, yet success criterion 3 requires it.

4. Title: Behaviour when one channel fails is undefined, and the claim that the marker "covers both" is incomplete. Severity P2. Location: summary ("the existing once-per-appointment marker covers both"), phase-2/t1 ("after the email and before markReminded"), and context.constraints.
Failure: In src/reminders/pass.ts:28-41, any throw skips markReminded (line 37) and only calls reportFailure (line 40).
- If the SMS send throws, the email has already gone out but the appointment stays unreminded. Any pass whose window still contains the appointment sends the email again. That window is [now+24h, now+24h+15m) (lines 23-25), and tests/pass.test.ts:15-17 already runs passes 5 minutes apart over the same appointment. That breaks request item 2: no second email.
- If the email send throws, the SMS is never attempted, so a valid mobile gets nothing.
Whether duplicates happen in production depends on how the scheduler lines up its runs (UNVERIFIED: the scheduler is not in this repo). The ordering problem inside the code is certain.
Fix: Decide and state the semantics. For example: send each channel independently, catch and report per channel, and mark reminded once after both attempts, so a failed channel can never cause a re-send of the other. Add tests:
- the SMS gateway throws: one email, appointment marked, failure reported, and a second pass sends nothing;
- the mailer throws: the SMS still goes out.
Also decide what the returned count means when one channel fails (pass.ts:21).

5. Title: The SMS fake and its test wiring are under-specified. Severity P2. Location: phase-2/t1 files tests/fakes.ts and tests/pass.test.ts.
Failure: fakeDeps' return type is hard-coded to `ReminderDeps & { emails; failures }` (tests/fakes.ts:11). Adding a required `sms` to ReminderDeps (pass.ts:7-14) breaks type-checking until fakes.ts gains `sms: SmsGateway` and returns an `sms: Sent[]` array. The plan mentions this only in passing. The failure tests in finding 4 also need a way to make a channel throw, which fakeDeps cannot do today.
Fix: Spell out the fakeDeps change: an `sms` array on the return type, plus an option for a failing mailer or gateway.

Verified as stated in the plan:
- formatSlot has exactly one production caller, pass.ts:34 (grep), plus tests/format.test.ts:5.
- Clinic carries an IANA timeZone (clinics.ts:5).
- SmsGateway is `send(to, text)` (gateway.ts:2-4).
- The marker is set after the messages go out (pass.ts:37).
- A patient without an email gets no email (pass.ts:30).
- The SMS text in the plan matches REQUEST.md.
- Phase-2's "second pass five minutes later sends nothing" scenario is consistent with the fake store (fakes.ts:19-25).

No elegance issues beyond the findings above: one formatSlot shared by both channels is the right shape.",
 "files_modified": []
}

Every code claim in plan.md checks out against the code: the Loan fields and the LoanStore port (src/loans.ts:3-17); Loan.renewals counting desk and online renewals (src/loans.ts:8); isOnHold and activeHolds dropping a hold once expiresOn has passed (src/holds.ts:15-22); IsoDate string comparison, addDays and todayIn (src/dates.ts:1-13); LIBRARY_TIME_ZONE (src/config.ts:2); Session.patronId (src/web/routes.ts:3-5); memoryLoans and memoryHolds (tests/fakes.ts:4-20). The rule order and the use of `today` for both the overdue and hold checks are sound.

Title: The plan requires a `dueOn` body that the existing account page does not send, so every online renewal would fail with 400
Severity: P1
Location: phase-1/t1 (shownDueOn parameter, already-renewed reason), phase-2/t1 (body `{ dueOn }`, "A body without a string dueOn is 400"), phase-2 qualitative_verification
Failure: Speculative Code / Leaky Interface. The page that calls these routes is a separate front end outside this repository. README.md:3 and README.md:10 say it only "shows the due date and a Renew button that posts to the loan's renew route". Nothing says it sends a body. The plan makes `{ dueOn }` mandatory, rejects requests without it (400), and has no task or owner for changing the front end. As planned, every renewal from the current page gets a 400, so rule-compliant renewals cannot happen and success criterion 1 fails. The staging check ("renew one loan") would fail the same way.
The guard itself (shownDueOn / already-renewed) defends against a risk the request never mentions: double-submits or stale pages. The plan gives one clause of rationale and no evidence that this happens. It adds a parameter, a reason, a message, a 409 path and two test scenarios. It also gives a misleading answer for a malformed value: dueOn "x" returns 409 "This loan was already renewed." (`loan.dueOn !== shownDueOn`).
Fix: Remove shownDueOn, the already-renewed reason and its message, and the 400 body check, along with their test scenarios (phase-1 scenario 6, phase-2 scenarios 4 and 5, and "a repeated request" in d2). The route becomes `postRenewal(deps, session, loanId, now)` with no body. If the lending team wants protection against double-submits, raise it as an open question with evidence (for example, logs of duplicate POSTs). If they confirm it, add a front-end change and its owner to the plan before making the field required.

 "summary": "Findings: the plan fails two of the four requirements. Requirement 3 fails because the plan's main claim about the code is false. Requirement 4 fails because the plan writes the watermark before the upload, and it says so on purpose.

F1. Title: Payment-sync status changes are never exported
Severity: P1
Location: context.key_files (src/members.ts entry), phase-1/t1, context.constraints[1]
Failure: The plan says the store stamps updatedAt on every write, including setStatus. The code says otherwise. src/members.ts:37 reads "The payment sync's write. It is not an officer's edit, so 'last edited' does not move." At src/members.ts:39, setStatus builds `{ ...this.get(id), status }` and leaves updatedAt alone. src/members.ts:11 documents updatedAt as the officer's "last edited" time, which the admin list shows. tests/members.test.ts:4-14 asserts that a lapsed write keeps the earlier updatedAt (line 14: `expect(lapsed.updatedAt).toEqual(edited)`). So `changedSince` on updatedAt never selects a member that the sync lapsed or cancelled, and requirement 3 fails. The constraint "member store and payment sync do not change" blocks the obvious fix, and stamping updatedAt in setStatus would break the "last edited" meaning and the existing test. The t1 scenario "payment sync set to lapsed after since is selected" can only pass with hand-built Member objects that carry a fresh updatedAt, so it tests a fiction.
Fix: Choose a change signal that exists. Preferred, because it needs no store change and meets the plan's constraint: save a snapshot of the last successfully exported rows in Settings, as one key mapping member_id to the CSV row or its hash. Export each member whose current row differs from the snapshot, and replace the snapshot only after a successful upload. This one mechanism covers the first run (empty snapshot), officer edits, status changes and failed uploads, and it drops the watermark. The alternative is to drop the constraint and add a separate `changedAt` field that create, update and setStatus all stamp, leaving updatedAt as "last edited". Either way, replace the t1 and phase-2 scenarios with one that drives a real MemberStore through setStatus and asserts the next export carries that member.

F2. Title: A failed upload loses its changes
Severity: P1
Location: phase-2/t1 description
Failure: The plan stores startedAt as the new watermark before calling uploadMembers. src/federation/client.ts:5 and :16 show uploadMembers throwing FederationError on a refused upload, and src/scheduler.ts:4 shows the scheduler only logging the error and running again the next night. That next run reads the moved watermark and skips every change the failed upload carried, which breaks requirement 4. The plan's stated reason is backwards. Sending the same full rows twice is harmless; losing changes is the failure the request names. Nothing in the repo shows that runs can overlap, since a nightly job runs 24 hours apart.
Fix: Write the watermark (or snapshot, under F1's fix) only after uploadMembers resolves, and let FederationError propagate to the scheduler. Delete the "slow upload" sentence. Add the scenario: "an upload that throws leaves the watermark unchanged, and the next run uploads the same members plus any new changes".

F3. Title: Directives and success criteria leave out requirements 3 and 4
Severity: P2
Location: implementation_contract.directives d1, success_criteria, phase-2/t1 test_scenarios
Failure: The d1 completion check covers only the first, incremental and empty runs. No directive, success criterion or job-level test covers the failed-upload requirement, and none covers a status change made through the real setStatus path. The plan could pass every check it defines while failing F1 and F2.
Fix: Add directives with completion checks for (a) a member changed by setStatus to lapsed or cancelled appears in the next export, using a real MemberStore, and (b) a failed upload does not advance the export state, and the next run resends those members.

F4. Title: Nothing calls registerJobs
Severity: P2
Location: phase-2/t2, directive d2
Failure: The repo has no entrypoint or composition root. The only sources are src/members.ts, settings.ts, scheduler.ts and federation/client.ts. Scheduler is an interface with no implementation (src/scheduler.ts:3-6). The plan adds registerJobs in a new src/jobs.ts but names no caller, so a test that registerJobs calls nightly does not prove that "the export runs nightly".
Fix: Name the production startup that will call registerJobs with the real Scheduler, Settings adapter and httpFederationClient. If that startup lives outside this repo, say so explicitly. Otherwise narrow d2 to "registerJobs registers the job" and record the wiring as a dependency.

F5. Title: The plan cites project patterns that the repo does not contain
Severity: P3
Location: context.patterns
Failure: "Jobs take their dependencies as one deps object and a clock" and "Persistent service state goes through Settings under a dotted key" have no basis in the code. No job exists, and nothing reads or writes Settings; src/settings.ts:2-5 is only the interface. These read as established conventions but are new decisions.
Fix: Restate them as design choices this plan makes.

F6. Title: The qualitative check names a test registry the repo does not have
Severity: P3
Location: phase-2.qualitative_verification
Failure: "Run against the federation's test registry" has no URL, credentials source or config in the repo. httpFederationClient(baseUrl, apiKey) at src/federation/client.ts:8 takes both from its caller, so the step cannot be carried out as written.
Fix: Name the registry base URL and where its API key comes from. If no test registry is available, replace the step with a local HTTP stub that captures the POST body and content-type sent to /registry/members (client.ts:11-14).

Checked and correct: the four CSV columns and their order match the request, assuming membership_type maps from membershipType (members.ts:8). The quoting rule in phase-1/t2 is right for RFC 4180 CSV. An absent watermark meaning the epoch does send everyone on the first run. Reading startedAt before members.all() with an inclusive (>=) comparison does not drop writes made between the two calls; it only resends them next run.",
